contract.proves:
Verify the safe rolling-maintenance discipline for a three-member control
plane: remove exactly one member, prove majority writes still work, restore
full quorum, and only then remove the next member.

This is the safety-dual of catastrophic/rolling-quorum-collapse.yaml. That
scenario proves that taking a second member down before the first member has
recovered destroys quorum. This scenario proves the intended operator rule:
never advance a control-plane maintenance window until the previous member is
healthy and caught up.

node-1 remains running because the harness uses node-1 as its etcd probe
anchor. The scenario rolls node-2 and node-3 and requires full 3/3 health
between disruptions.

What this validates:
  - 2/3 Raft quorum remains writable during each single-member outage
  - a restarted member catches up before the next maintenance step begins
  - repeated membership turnover does not leave stale health or registration
    state behind
  - the cluster finishes with full quorum and write availability
